messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
Hello all,

I am running a spatially coefficient varying model for a spatiotemporal data with missing values for both the outcome and covariates. My formula is 

formula2 <- U5MR ~ f(OBJECTID, model = "bym2", graph = Global.adj.path, scale.model = TRUE) + 
  f(OBJECTID2, model="iid") +
  f(Year, model = "iid") + 
  f(Yr_id, model = "rw1") + 
  f(CNT_time_id, model = "iid") +
  f(ID_SEC, SEC, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_FEMP, FEMP, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) +
  f(ID_GDP, GDP, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_OPH, OPH, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_HEXP, HEXP, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_WATER, WATER, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_DEF, DEF, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_SANI, SANI, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) + 
  f(ID_PM, PM2.5, model = "besag", graph = Global.adj.path, constr=F) 

and the model 

model2 <- inla(formula2, family="gaussian", data=DF,
               control.predictor=list(compute=T), 
               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE, keep=TRUE)

I got an error message stating 
"Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
In addition: Warning message:
In inla.model.properties.generic(inla.trim.family(model), mm[names(mm) ==  :
  Model 'bym2' in section 'latent' is marked as 'experimental'; changes may appear at any time."
  Use this model with extra care!!! Further warnings are disabled.

A message prior this error information contains the following details

GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Function  : GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern
File      : approx-inference.c
Line      : 2972
GitID     : file: approx-inference.c  dde623981a9591b2d3f82188ac0b6f962078ccb9 - Fri Aug 21 15:53:46 2020 +0300

Any help on how to resolve this would be greatly appreciated. Regards,


NB: When a model with fixed effect and random effect for spatial units (using the formula and model below), it runs fine with no issues.

formula1 <- U5MR ~ SEC + FEMP + GDP + OPH + HEXP + WATER + DEF + SANI + PM2.5 +
  f(OBJECTID, model = "bym2", graph = Global.adj.path, scale.model = TRUE) + 
  f(OBJECTID2, model="iid") +
  f(Year, model = "iid") + 
  f(Yr_id, model = "rw1") + 
  f(CNT_time_id, model = "iid")
model1 <- inla(formula1, family="gaussian", data=DF,
               control.predictor=list(compute=T), 
               control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE, keep=TRUE)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
Hi, with a such model then its easy to run into hidden confounding
issues. you may try with setting

f(..., model="besag", scale.model=TRUE,
hyper=list(prec=list(prior="pc.prec",
param=c(1,0.01))))

then scale covariates SEC FEMP etc..., and add in one by one, and add

control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=1)

or similar.

H
